title: Beamed stem lengths and beam slant
description: Beamed groups whose outer heads span a third, a fifth and an octave, one, two and three beams deep, with one down-stem octave at each of the first two depths, then groups built to exercise the slant rules. Pins the beam-geometry rule (roadmap: core-beam-geometry, as amended): the stem that would come out shortest lands on the minimum of 2.5 spaces whatever the beam count, and every other stem grows from there; the beam is flat when the outer heads match, when the heads form a repeating pattern, or when the head nearest the beam is an inner one, and otherwise rises a quarter space per staff step of the outer interval, capped at three quarters; and the primary beam then nudges outward until it sits on, straddles or hangs from a staff line. Bars 1–4 are alternating patterns and beam flat: bar 1 eighths, a third then a fifth; bar 2 eighths, an octave up-stem then an octave down-stem; bar 3 sixteenths, third / fifth / octave / octave down-stem, one group per beat; bar 4 thirty-seconds, a third then an octave, then a half rest. Bar 5 sixteenths: a rising fifth (slants up to the cap), an inner-extreme group (flat), a falling fourth (slants down), a falling step with its inner heads on the lower note (a quarter-space slant). Bar 6 eighths: a rising fourth, then a group whose inner head is level with the nearer outer one (flat). Bar 7: a falling step in eighths, then rests.
